reach.rationale: No experimental/preview/RC APIs at all, but the app leans entirely on APIs that only became stable four weeks ago (SvelteKit 3 config surface, `#lib` alias, renamed goto options) in central places — squarely the 'recently-stable in central places' anchor.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7-15 — the whole Kit-3-specific config surface is confined to one file
app/package.json:24-26 — `#lib` alias is declared once in the imports field, mechanically replaceable
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:49 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.svelte:16 — the only Kit-3-named navigation options appear in two components
app/src/routes/+layout.svelte:2 — `#lib/*` import specifiers, however, appear in nearly every module (e.g. +page.server.ts:1, MoveTable imports), so a future change would touch many files
containment.rationale: The recently-stable Kit 3 surface is mostly confined to three config files plus two goto call sites, and there is nothing experimental to contain; the only spread is the `#lib` specifier string, which is a single find-and-replace and the framework's forward standard.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7-13 — adapter/compilerOptions must live in the vite plugin in Kit 3; svelte.config.js is no longer supported (migration guide)
app/package.json:24-26 — `#lib` is required: Kit 3 no longer generates the `$lib` alias
app/src/routes/+page.svelte:49 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/+page.svelte:16 — `replace`/`reset` are the only names the current release accepts (old goto option names removed)
app/vite.config.ts:10 — runes-as-function mirrors the compiler docs' guidance to avoid forcing runes onto node_modules; option is documented and stable
app/src/routes/+page.server.ts:8 — chose mature server load functions over Kit's still-experimental remote functions, which bought nothing here
justification.rationale: Every newly-stable API used has no surviving long-stable alternative in the current release — these are mandatory conventions, not novelty — and the one genuinely experimental feature (remote functions) was avoided, so nothing is gratuitous.

findings.issue: The entire dependency set sits on majors released ~4 weeks before this review (SvelteKit 3, adapter-node 6, vite-plugin-svelte 7, Vite 8, TypeScript 6) with caret ranges, and patch churn is active (kit 3.0.1/3.1.0/3.1.1 and svelte 5.57.2→5.57.3 within October 2026).
findings.suggestion: This is the current stable release and the right target, so no change is needed — just rely on the committed lockfile for builds and schedule dependency updates rather than relying on caret drift in CI.

findings.issue: The `runes` function-form compile option forces runes mode and is, per its own comment, a transitional knob slated to be removable in Svelte 6 (where runes become the default).
findings.suggestion: Keep it for now (it is documented and stable), but track the Svelte 6 release and delete the option once forced runes is the default, to avoid carrying a stale compile setting for years.

summary: The app contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs: no experimental config flags, no unstable names, and no beta-tagged dependencies in its own dependency tree. Its only novelty exposure is that it is built entirely on the SvelteKit 3 / Vite 8 / TypeScript 6 stack that reached stable release on 2026-10-01, using Kit 3's now-mandatory conventions (vite-plugin config, `#lib` imports, renamed `goto` options) idiomatically and with correct handling of Kit 3's readonly `page.url`. Notably, it avoided the framework's still-experimental remote functions in favour of mature `+page.server.ts` load functions, so residual risk is limited to the youth of the platform versions themselves.
